title: Non-exchangeable Conformal Prediction for Temporal Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Temporal dependencies in graph structure, node attributes, and ground truth labels violate the exchangeability assumption required by standard conformal prediction methods, limiting their applicability to temporal graphs.

gap.claim: Existing conformal prediction methods for graph neural networks predominantly focus on static graphs and neglect evolving real-world graphs.

contributions.claim: NCPNET is an end-to-end conformal prediction framework tailored for temporal graphs.
The framework uses a diffusion-based non-conformity score that captures topological and temporal uncertainties in evolving networks.
The framework includes an efficiency-aware optimization algorithm intended to improve computational efficiency and reduce coverage violations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe NCPNET as a novel framework for conformal prediction on temporal graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on WIKI, REDDIT, DBLP, and IBM Anti-Money Laundering temporal graphs reportedly demonstrate guaranteed coverage in temporal graphs.
On the WIKI dataset, the authors report up to a 31% reduction in prediction set size and improved efficiency compared with state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that their data and code are publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conformal prediction is presented as a framework for quantifying uncertainty and improving GNN reliability in high-stakes applications.
Existing methods focus mainly on static graphs, while temporal dependencies violate standard exchangeability assumptions.
The authors introduce NCPNET, extend conformal prediction to dynamic settings, and propose diffusion-based uncertainty scoring.
An efficiency-aware optimization algorithm is proposed to improve computation and reduce coverage violations.
Experiments across four real-world temporal graph datasets are reported to show coverage, smaller prediction sets, and improved efficiency; data and code are reported as available.

source_observation.claim: Temporal dependencies can invalidate exchangeability assumptions used by standard conformal prediction.

interpretation.claim: Uncertainty methods applied to evolving data may require calibration procedures that explicitly model temporal dependence.

application.claim: When deploying conformal prediction on temporal graphs, assess whether graph structure, attributes, and labels are temporally dependent before relying on standard coverage assumptions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when standard exchangeability assumptions remain adequate for temporal graphs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal coverage guarantee or its conditions.
The abstract does not describe the diffusion-based score or optimization algorithm in sufficient technical detail.
The abstract does not report experimental protocols, baseline identities, statistical uncertainty, or results beyond the stated WIKI reduction.
